newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico net international assets slightly lower.
newsitem.headline: Mexico net international assets slightly lower.

text.p: Banco de Mexico said Tuesday its net international assets as of December 6 were $5.016 billion, compared with $5.023 billion on November 29.
The central bank said that its international reserves as of December 6 were $16.398 billion, compared with $16.317 billion as of November 29.
It said the decrease of $7 million in international assets in the week was due to:
- Net revenues from operations with state oil firm Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex) worth $150 million
- Purchases of $110 million from credit institutions who exercised dollar put options following a November 29 options auction
- Net sales of foreign currency to the federal government worth $239 million for foreign debt service payments

- A net loss of $28 million from a combination of factors including changes in the dollar value of non-dollar assets and liabilities held by the bank; net returns on interest rates and from trading of metals and securities; and net deposits in dollar accounts of commercial banks at the central bank.
Banco de Mexico said the monetary base rose by 5.013 billion pesos due to a seasonal rise in demand for notes and coins.

The balance of the government's deposits with the central bank fell by 9.642 billion pesos, mainly as a result of transfers of funds from the central government to the states, payments of Christmas bonuses to teachers and foreign debt service payments.
Central bank credit to financial institutions fell by 4.657 billion pesos to compensate for the monetary impact of the fall in government deposits with the central bank.
The following tables detail Banco de Mexico's assets and net domestic credit. All figures are in billions of pesos, unless otherwise indicated.
*Net International Assets are defined as gross international assets minus central bank liabilities with the IMF and assets of less than a six month duration from other central banks.
